Misao Okawa, who was 117 years old, has died. She was the oldest person in the world according to Guinness World Records.

Okawa passed away on Wednesday in Osaka, Japan. She is survived by three children, four grandchildren, and six great-grandchildren. She was born on March 5, 1898.

Her family ran a kimono shop in Osaka. A worker at the nursing home where she lived said Okawa had a gentle personality and loved to eat. Her favorite foods were sushi and udon noodles. She ate a lot of cake to celebrate her birthday on March 5 last year.

Washington (CNN) The Missouri National Guard prepared to deploy to help stop riots in Ferguson, Missouri, that happened sporadically last year. The guard used strong, military words like "enemy forces" and "adversaries" to describe the protesters. The guard went to Ferguson to help police officers. Many community leaders and civil rights activists said the police used too much force and made a bad situation worse. The protests started in August and continued sporadically until the end of the year.

Gunmen attacked the Somalia education ministry in Mogadishu on Tuesday. A suicide car bombing happened at the entrance first. Then, five gunmen went inside and started shooting.

The attack killed at least 12 people and injured 16 others. The Islamist group Al-Shabaab took responsibility for the attack. The ministry building houses Education, Culture, and Higher Education.

One war was enough for Gregory Margolin. Now 87 years old, he was a 16-year-old Jewish recruit who fought in the Soviet Red Army against the Nazis in World War II. His family fled during the conflict, but Margolin did not reveal he was Jewish because "people were being killed left and right" all around him.

This year, in Ukraine, he found himself surrounded by war again. Margolin was a sniper who eventually became a commander. His old uniform is still decorated with military medals. His granddaughter Liora is amazed that he survived the fighting.

More than 200 Nigerian schoolgirls disappeared from their boarding school in Chibok, northeastern Nigeria, exactly one year ago. They were taken from their dormitories in the middle of the night by armed men. The girls are still missing. This event should make everyone feel ashamed. It shows that in our world, young girls can have their lives destroyed by violent fanatics without any consequences. It is also shameful that the world’s attention on this tragedy has been very short-lived.

In Norway, digital radio is replacing FM radio. By 2027, the country will be the first in the world to stop using FM broadcasts completely. Norwegians won't lose radio entirely; they will just need to switch to digital. Officials say many of the country's 5 million people have already made the change. On FM, listeners can only find five stations. On Digital Audio Broadcasting, there are twenty stations. Half the country already listens to radio digitally, said Culture Minister Thorhild Widvey.

Everybody loves a good comeback story, especially one about a dinosaur. For over 100 years, the Brontosaurus was removed from science books. However, a new study suggests it is its own kind of dinosaur and should have its own name.

O.C. Marsh first named the Brontosaurus in 1879. He named it after he received 25 crates of bones found at Como Bluff, Wyoming, according to the Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History. The Brontosaurus is similar to, but not as large as, the Apatosaurus, which was discovered a few years earlier. Marsh named the dinosaur "Brontosaurus," which means "thunder lizard."

Al Qaeda in Yemen is offering a reward of 20 kilograms of gold to anyone who kills or captures two men. The men are Abdelmalik Bedrudin Al-Houthi, the leader of the rebels who took over Yemen's capital, and former President Ali Abdullah Saley. The gold is worth about $774,000. Al Qaeda calls the two men the "two heads of evil." Several groups are fighting to control Yemen.

Before landing a gyrocopter on the Capitol lawn Wednesday, Doug Hughes wrote about his intentions and the reasons behind them on a website called thedemocracyclub.org. "The point of the flight is to spotlight corruption in DC and more importantly, to present the solution(s) to the institutional graft," the 61-year-old Florida postal carrier wrote in an online post titled "Your Pilot." "My flight is not a secret," the post says. "Before I took off, I sent an Email to info@barackobama.com. The letter is intended to persuade the guardians of the Capitol that I am not a threat and that shooting me down will be a bigger headache than letting me deliver these letters to Congress."

Bad news for Rio de Janeiro before the 2016 Olympics continues. Scores of dead fish appeared in the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon. With just over a year until the Games start, the legislative assembly of Rio de Janeiro started an investigation into why fish are dying in the lagoon and other lakes and bays in the state. The group will work with the State Environmental Institute and the Secretariat of State for the Environment.

Anthony Ray Hinton is 58 years old. He spent nearly 30 years in jail on Alabama's death row. Until recently, he was in a small 5-by-7 foot cell most of the time. Last week, his murder convictions were removed, and he was freed from a Birmingham jail. Hinton told CNN that he has to pinch himself to remember he is free, and that he is still getting used to the idea.

A poll about the UK election debate between seven party leaders found no clear winner. The results were as follows:

*   **Comres for ITV:** David Cameron, Ed Miliband, and Nigel Farage were tied for first place with 21% each. Nicola Sturgeon was close behind with 20%.
*   **ICM for The Guardian:** Ed Miliband scored 25%, David Cameron scored 24%, Nigel Farage scored 19%, and Nicola Sturgeon scored 17%.

A New York judge has ruled that Facebook is an acceptable way to serve divorce papers. Ellanora Arthur Baidoo has been trying to divorce her husband, Victor Sena Blood-Dzraku, for several years. Her lawyer, Andrew Spinnell, could not find Mr. Blood-Dzraku to give him the papers. However, Mr. Blood-Dzraku has told Ms. Baidoo by phone that he has no fixed address and no job.

It sounds like a science fiction movie. A person has a terrible accident and goes to the hospital. They are brain dead and on life support. Doctors ask the family about organ donation. Usually, this saves up to eight lives. But in this case, the family is asked to donate the whole body to save just one person. This person might be quadriplegic, meaning they cannot move their body, but their mind works fine.

It sounds crazy, but Italian doctor Sergio Canavero says we can do it. He calls the project HEAVEN. This stands for head anastomosis venture. Anastomosis means surgically connecting two parts. The goal is to put an entire head on a new body.

CNN reported that Anthony Stokes, a heart transplant recipient, died on Tuesday after leading police on a high-speed chase and crashing his car into a pole. In 2013, an Atlanta hospital rejected him for heart surgery because of his "history of non-compliance," according to a letter from the hospital. At that time, Mark Bell was speaking for the Stokes family.

It was very early in the morning at Garissa University College. Most students were still sleeping. A few had woken up to go to Christian prayers. Suddenly, there was an explosion and gunfire at the school's front gates around 5:30 a.m. on Thursday. The attackers continued to shoot as they moved through the campus. The Red Cross said they stopped at a girls' dormitory. At one point, the attackers burst into a room where Christians were gathered and took them hostage, according to lecturer Joel Ayora.

A white casket was at the front of New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore. A gospel choir sang for a large crowd gathered to honor Freddie Gray. The 25-year-old died in police custody 15 days ago after he was arrested on a weapons charge. His death from a severe spinal cord injury sparked widespread outrage toward the Baltimore Police Department. Gray's death in custody is the latest in a string of high-profile deaths involving African-Americans and law enforcement. Many have demanded answers about what happened to Gray, and his funeral drew civil rights leaders, politicians, and relatives of others who died in police custody.

I have been a chef since I was 14. In 2007, my wife mentored a young girl who was forced to search through trash to find food. This inspired me to start Food Policy Action and work on issues like hunger and factory farms.

I am not alone in this work. A major catalyst was "The Meatrix," a 2003 cartoon that parodies "The Matrix." Produced by the GRACE Communications Foundation, it highlighted the public health risks and environmental damage caused by factory farming.

Dan Swangard is a doctor who has seen many patients die in hospitals. He has seen them hooked up to morphine and struggling with fear. He has watched death drag on for weeks or months while terrified relatives stood by.

Recently, this changed. In 2013, Swangard was diagnosed with a rare, metastatic cancer. To treat it, surgeons removed parts of his pancreas and liver, as well as his spleen and gallbladder. The surgery was successful. However, Swangard, who is 48, knows there is a strong chance the cancer will return.

Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters fight against the Houthis and their allies in Aden. The special forces were on the ground in noncombat roles, coordinating and guiding the battle. They also helped parachute in weapons and communications equipment.

Following heavy Saudi airstrikes, Houthi rebels withdrew from the presidential palace and other key parts of the southern port city of Aden. This withdrawal marked a reversal from the previous day, when Houthi forces had seized the presidential palace.

A Detroit mother was arrested last month after police found two dead children inside a freezer. She was charged this week with murder and torture.

Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy charged Mitchelle Angela Blair with killing her 13-year-old daughter, Stoni Ann Blair, and her 9-year-old son, Stephen Gage Berry.

According to Detroit Police Chief James Craig, a bailiff found the bodies wrapped in plastic during a court-ordered eviction on March 24. The medical examiner says Stoni died from blunt force injuries, and Stephen died from blunt force and heat injuries.

Miami (CNN) - World heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko has an important fight coming up on April 25 against Bryant Jennings in New York. However, his mind is on the crisis in Ukraine. Speaking from his Miami training base, Klitschko said the situation in his homeland has shocked and upset him. He stated that his country is suffering because of a war with Russia, and that Ukraine has not been the aggressor.

Michael Keaton hosted "Saturday Night Live" for the third time this weekend. He made small references to his famous roles as Beetlejuice and Batman.

In his opening speech, Keaton joked that a lot has changed since 1982. He mentioned he has a 31-year-old son and a new girlfriend who is 28.

Fans wanted Keaton to act out his famous characters, but the show's cast only got him to say a few short jokes.

Just over a month ago, a jury found Kamron Taylor guilty of murder. Early Wednesday morning, Taylor was hiding in an Illinois jail. He jumped out and attacked a correctional officer who was walking around. He beat the guard, took his uniform and keys, and walked out of the jail. He then got into the officer's brown 2012 Chevrolet Equinox SUV. The 23-year-old, who was supposed to be sentenced in May, is now missing. Police found the SUV around 8:30 a.m.

A New York City detective has been suspended after police accused him of stealing $3,000 during a raid on a store that sells illegal cigarettes.

Surveillance video from News 12 Brooklyn shows Detective Ian Cyrus putting cash into a bag at the Yemen Deli and Grocery store in Brooklyn last Friday. The detectives had arrested two store employees for selling loose cigarettes. The store manager, Ali Abdullah, noticed money was missing from a box. He checked the security cameras and saw the detective take the money, which he could not believe.

Thieves broke into a famous safe deposit company in London over a holiday weekend. They used special tools and ropes to get into the vault. They went through many boxes and stole gems and cash. Experts believe they took hundreds of thousands of pounds, and one former police official thinks they may have taken as much as 200 million pounds ($300 million).

As South Africa marks the 30th anniversary of its first post-apartheid elections on April 27, 1994, deadly attacks against African migrants are happening again. Outrage over this violence is spreading on social media with the hashtag #WeAreAfrica, showing the need for unity. These attacks on migrants and their property suggest that the country's "rainbow nation" dream has failed. That vision promised a multi-ethnic society where people of all races and classes could live with dignity.

In 1989, Ayatollah Khomeini called accepting a ceasefire "drinking poison" to end the eight-year war with Iraq. The war had defined his newly founded Islamic Republic. Khomeini encouraged both his supporters and opponents to fight the enemy, dragging out the conflict for eight years despite Iraq's willingness to end it. This stabilized his regime. However, by the time the war ended, the economy was ruined and his volunteers had disappeared.

The idea of sustainable development is that raw capitalism is too powerful. Global capitalism is a huge force, with the world economy doubling in size every generation. Yet on a finite Earth, with a billion new people added every 15 years, this force is now attacking the physical bases of life and the social systems that make life pleasant. Sustainable development offers a path out of this growing crisis. The reality is that raw capitalism is the economics of greed.

The United States benefits from being a space-faring nation. U.S. access to space helps national security, the military, and the economy. To fight terrorism and other global threats, the military relies on satellites for intelligence, GPS, and communications. However, the U.S. is in a difficult position because it relies too heavily on Russian technology to meet its national security needs.

On the one-year anniversary of the abduction of nearly 300 schoolgirls in Nigeria, Malala Yousafzai wrote an open letter to them. Malala, who is 17, survived an attack by the Taliban in Pakistan because she blogged about the importance of girls going to school. In her letter, she asks the Nigerian government and the world to do more to find the girls. Nigeria recently held an election.

CNN reports that South African soldiers were sent out Tuesday night to help stop deadly attacks against foreigners. Their first stop was the Johannesburg area of Jeppestown, where violence started on Friday. Police raided a hostel in Jeppestown Tuesday, while soldiers guarded the area. Defense Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula said the government is sending an unknown number of soldiers to places where police are too spread out to stop the attacks. She said, "This intervention is not an indictment on the police."

Eight Iranian border guards were killed in clashes with militants near the Pakistan border. Three militants were also killed in the fighting that happened on Monday in Negur, a town in southeastern Iran. Iran's deputy governor, Ali Asghar Mirshekari, said the militants crossed into Iran from Pakistan. Iranian officials have asked Pakistani authorities to arrest the surviving attackers.

TripAdvisor named Providenciales in the Turks and Caicos the world's best island. The island moved up from second place last year, pushing Ambergris Caye in Belize out of the top spot. Ambergris Caye had been number one for two years, but fell out of the top ten entirely this year. TripAdvisor says it is hard to explain why islands drop in the rankings, as the results change every year based on traveler feedback.

CNN reported that details about the 2016 movie "Star Wars: Rogue One" were shared at a fan festival in Anaheim, California. Director Gareth Edwards showed a preview of the film and explained the story. This movie is part of the "Star Wars" series, but Disney calls it an "anthology film" instead of a "spinoff." The story takes place between the third and fourth movies. It follows a group of rebels who go on a dangerous mission to steal the plans for the Death Star. Felicity Jones plays a rebel soldier in the film.

Tehran, Iran (CNN)

There is a Persian proverb that says: "A good year is determined by its spring." For many Iranians, the historic decision by Tehran and six world powers -- the United States, Britain, France, Germany, Russia and China -- to continue nuclear negotiations is an indication that this year's Norouz, the Persian New Year that started on March 21, will be a very good one. Although some hardliners may complain that the preliminary agreement is not what they wanted, for many people it shows excellent progress.

Ferguson, Missouri (CNN) -- Two African-American women, Ella Jones and Wesley Bell, were elected to the Ferguson City Council on Tuesday. This means three of the six council members are now black. The election took place on Tuesday, following a previous story published earlier in the day.

The voting began at 6 a.m. Despite ominous skies and warnings of flash floods, voters turned out in record numbers. This was the first city election since August of last year, when white police Officer Darren Wilson shot and killed unarmed black teenager Michael Brown. Since that event, voter turnout in Ferguson had been very low, but Tuesday's election saw a significant increase in participation.

An Israeli man was killed and a woman was injured in a suspected terror attack near Hebrew University in Jerusalem on Wednesday night. Police say a 37-year-old Arab man from East Jerusalem drove his car into two people standing at a bus stop in the French Hill area. One victim, identified as Shalom Yohai Cherki, 26, died at the hospital. A 20-year-old woman is in serious condition. The driver was arrested and is being investigated by the General Security Services.

A collection of art owned by the late actress Lauren Bacall was sold in New York on March 31. The collection includes works by famous 20th-century artists. It was shown in Hong Kong, Paris, London, and Los Angeles before the sale. Bacall died in 2014 at age 89. She became famous in 1944 with the movie "To Have And Have Not," where she met her husband, Humphrey Bogart. At the 2015 Golden Globes, George Clooney honored her.

Kiev, Ukraine (CNN) People in Kiev are asking who is killing friends of Ukraine's removed President Viktor Yanukovych. This is not a new idea, but it became important again this week. Two important people were shot and killed in the Ukrainian capital. One was a former member of parliament, Oleg Kalashnikov, who had ties to Yanukovych. The other was a Ukrainian journalist known for supporting Russia. Kalashnikov was shot and killed at the door of his apartment building on Wednesday evening.

CNN reports that Chile will soon recognize civil unions for same-sex couples. President Michelle Bachet signed a new law on Monday to make this happen. She said this is a step toward treating homosexual and heterosexual couples equally. The law will officially start in six months. It gives legal rights to couples who live together, whether they are two men, two women, or a man and a woman. The government believes about 2 million people will benefit from this change.

The next time you fly to Florida to visit Grandma, look out the window. Whether you are going to see a talking mouse at a theme park or heading to South Beach for sun and fun, look for a window seat. Before the plane lands in Miami or Orlando, you will see a huge, swampy area below. This is the Everglades. It looks like a wet, wild place full of dangerous animals like snakes, scorpions, rats, roaches, alligators, and mosquitoes. A researcher once caught 365,000 mosquitoes in one trap in just one night.

CNN reports that ISIS militants took control of Yarmouk, a Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus. The group stormed the area, flooding the streets. For over two years, the camp had been besieged and bombed by Syrian forces. In early April, ISIS defeated local militia groups. A resident told CNN that ISIS killed three people in the street. The resident said, "They slaughtered them in the streets." The resident added that the Islamic State now controls almost all of the camp.

China has long blocked its citizens from reading Western news using a "Great Firewall." But a new study says China has now created a "Great Cannon" to attack servers outside its borders, including in the United States. The study's authors say this visible attack will likely anger other countries, and China may have expected this reaction.

A German official said Monday that the investigation into the crash of Germanwings Flight 9525 has not found a clear reason why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed the plane. However, the official said Lubitz had suicidal thoughts before he became a pilot and received medical treatment for it.

Investigators have not found any notes or recordings where Lubitz explained his actions. Medical records show he was suicidal and saw a therapist, but this happened before he ever got his pilot's license.

The leader of Yemen's Houthi rebels said on Sunday that his group will not give up. He stated that his fighters will not leave the main cities or government buildings. He added that anyone expecting them to surrender is wrong.

This comes after more than three weeks of Saudi-led airstrikes. The goal of these bombings is to push back the Houthis. The rebels recently seized the capital, Sanaa, and removed President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power.

On April 19, 1995, Timothy McVeigh drove a truck bomb into the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The explosion killed 168 people and injured hundreds. It remains the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in U.S. history.

The attack shocked the nation. While the scale of the tragedy was huge, the real shock was that American citizens had turned their violence toward their own government. This was a new and frightening development for the country.

If you care about something, you might protest, make a sign, or join a demonstration. How long would you keep going if no one listened?

When more than 200 Nigerian girls were kidnapped from their school a year ago by Boko Haram militants, millions of people around the world joined a social media campaign to ask for their safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of those people, joining celebrities and world leaders who used the hashtag #BringBackOurGirls. This hashtag became one of the most popular on Twitter in 2014, appearing in more than four million tweets. However, as weeks turned into months, the missing girls were still not found. Eventually, the public's attention on the campaign faded.

Barney Frank is an experienced politician. At a recent event in Chicago, the retired congressman entertained a full house as he talked about his 45 years in public service. Frank made history by becoming the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same-sex while in office. He also had strong words for politicians who hide their identity while voting against gay rights. When an audience member asked about a California ballot proposal that would legalize killing gay people, Frank said he had not heard of the measure and told the young man not to worry about "crazy people."

A deadly attack at Garissa University College in Kenya left nearly 150 people dead and many others wounded. Gunmen attacked the campus early Thursday while students were praying, shooting randomly and taking hostages before security forces killed them. The U.S. Embassy confirmed that the Al-Shabaab militant group claimed responsibility. This attack follows a previous incident where Al-Shabaab killed non-Muslim workers at a Kenyan quarry. The group has carried out many other attacks in the region and has recruited some Americans, especially from the Somali-American community in Minnesota.

Students at the University of Cape Town in South Africa have removed a statue of British colonialist Cecil Rhodes. The students demanded the statue come down for weeks using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall, saying he was a racist. The university received permission from the heritage authority to take the statue down. They said the removal is to keep the statue safe while they decide what to do with it in the future.

Syria is a very dangerous place. An opposition group says the number of people who have died has doubled in one year. Since the civil war started, 310,000 people have been killed, according to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights. A year ago, that number was 162,402. The United Nations said the death toll was 70,000 the year before that. Over half of all Syrians are very poor and need help to survive. The United Nations says food rations have been cut because not enough people are donating money.

Ailina Tsarnaeva went to Manhattan Criminal Court. She was quiet and shy. However, prosecutors say she was not timid when it came to a rival.

According to court papers, Tsarnaeva called a woman this summer. She threatened the woman, saying, "Leave my man alone." She also said, "Stop looking for him. ... I know people that can put a bomb where you live."

Because of who she is, prosecutors did not think this was a joke. They charged her with aggravated harassment. Tsarnaeva denies the charge. She left court in December and would not talk about the case.

Tsarnaeva is the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev.

A police official in Gaza said on Thursday that a door with a drawing by the famous artist Banksy was taken by police. The owner, Rabea Darduna, went to court because he sold the door for only $175 without realizing how valuable it was. The door is now being held by Khan Younis police in southern Gaza. Darduna said that when his home was destroyed last summer, he was left with only a doorway and a door.

A Saudi-led group is attacking rebels in Yemen. The group says it is winning, but many people have left their homes because of the fighting. Many people have been hurt, including many civilians. Five days after the first attacks, the group destroyed the rebels' weapons that stop planes. They also made almost all of the places where planes take off and land unusable. Saudi Arabia's navy now controls the ports in Yemen. Only medical supplies that are not for fighting are allowed to enter.

Holland manager Guus Hiddink was very angry that his own fans booed Spain player Andres Iniesta during the 2-0 game on Tuesday. Spain coach Vicente del Bosque played an experimental team, and Iniesta came into the game in the 76th minute. The home fans jeered and booed him. Centre back Stefan de Vrij and midfielder Davy Klaassen scored the goals for Holland. Hiddink called the booing a "disgrace." Spain midfielder Andres Iniesta played in Holland's 2-0 defeat on Tuesday night.

Scotland will find out on May 21 if Georgia's September Euro 2016 qualifier will be played without fans in the stands. UEFA has opened an investigation against the Georgian Football Federation because fans twice ran onto the field during Sunday's 2-0 loss to Germany in Tbilisi. UEFA is also looking into charges that home fans set off fireworks. Other safety issues being investigated include blocked stairs, locked gates, and a lack of body searches by staff at the Boris Paichadze Stadium. A fan ran onto the pitch during Georgia's 2-0 defeat by Germany on Sunday in Tbilisi.

On Wednesday, football agents waited to hear about new rules. Starting April 1, anyone can become a football agent by paying £500 for a one-year registration. The FA will then charge £250 every year to renew it. Existing licensed agents were exempt from this. The FA was supposed to put a registration link on their website at 1pm, but it was not there yet. Mel Stein believes these new rules will cause chaos. The new guidelines started after FIFA stopped governing agents.

Financially-troubled CSKA Sofia's Latvian goalkeeper Maksims Uvarenko has not been paid for three months. He had to ask his parents to send him money to pay his rent. Despite the financial problems, Uvarenko, who joined the Bulgarian club on an 18-month contract in January, is impressed by the 'unique' fans and their passionate support. He told local media that the lack of money is the biggest problem he has faced at CSKA. He has not received any salary since joining the club three months ago.

David Moore, 25, got very angry while driving. He had just left his home and immediately found himself stuck in heavy traffic behind Rafal Cegielka, 45. Mr. Cegielka was picking up his child from St John's Primary School in Burnley, Lancashire. Mr. Moore then punched Mr. Cegielka and smashed up his car with a hockey stick. This happened in front of young children because Mr. Moore was having a "bad day" and lost his temper.

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday. This defeat reminded people of their bad performance at the 2014 World Cup. However, coach Vicente del Bosque is not worried about a third straight loss. This is what Gerard Pique said. Holland beat Spain 5-1 in the group stage of the World in Brazil last year. That game ended Spain's six-year time as the best team in the world. Holland scored two early goals at the Amsterdam Arena. They held on against Spain, who pressed them hard in the second half, for a 2-0 win.

A New York City mother and her daughter have fled to Germany during a custody dispute. Police say Ulrike Berger, 44, is not allowed to leave the country with her seven-year-old daughter, Kaia, due to a court order. However, on March 22, the day after Kaia was dropped off for a visit, they are believed to have flown to Europe.

Police are searching for Ulrike Berger and Kaia. It is believed they boarded a flight from New York to Germany on March 22, breaking the court order. The pair was last seen at Berger's home in Boerun Hill, Brooklyn, at 10:00 AM on March 21, when Kaia's father dropped her off.

A huge fire ripped through dry heathland near the south coast. Flames leaped up and acrid smoke billowed into the sky. The fire came after days of storms had lashed Britain, felling trees and shutting roads.

The fire burned about 70 hectares of land in Dorset. This area was very dry because it is on a hill, and rain had run off down the slope. The fire was started deliberately. It destroyed three separate areas of heath, measuring half a hectare, one hectare, and 70 hectares.

Last night, emergency services in Britain received 600 calls every hour because people were celebrating. Paramedics were very busy, and in Cambridge, a field hospital was set up to help drunk partygoers. At the busiest time, the London Ambulance Service was handling over 600 calls an hour—more than three times the usual amount.

In Manchester, a man collapsed on the pavement next to an ambulance while two people walked past eating food. Also in Manchester, a man was found slumped in a doorway while two women celebrated the New Year.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet was dropped from the team in December. Manager Brendan Rodgers dropped him because his performance was poor. However, Mignolet returned to the team after Brad Jones got hurt. Mignolet, who is 27, said his mental strength helped him recover. He told the magazine FourFourTwo that he stayed positive.

On Tuesday, giant hailstones the size of plums crashed down over the South. Residents rushed outside to capture the freak weather. In Bryant, Arkansas, Twitter user Arke USA filmed the ice balls hitting his backyard and splashing into his swimming pool. The footage shows the hailstones falling at high speed and cracking upon impact. Despite the temperature being around 80 degrees, the hail was resilient and took a while to melt. In seconds, the patio was completely covered in white pellets.

A replica pirate ship called the Liana's Ransom lost power in rough water off the coast of Maine on Monday. The crew had to jump into the water after their sails got tangled around the mast. The U.S. Coast Guard rescued nine people using life boats on Tuesday. The ship was left drifting about 30 miles east of Portland.

New photos show blue glowing algae lighting up a beach in Australia. The pictures were taken at Jervis Bay on the south coast of New South Wales. The glow came from millions of tiny plankton in the water. A photographer called the scene "beautiful and supernatural." A similar event happened at Manly Beach in Sydney back in 2014, and an expert said people did not need to worry.

A 17-year-old boy named Rahul Kumar climbed over a fence at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad, India, while he was drunk. He ran towards the lions in their enclosure, shouting that he would kill them. Zoo security had to rescue him. Mr. Kumar later explained that he was intoxicated and believed he could defeat the animals.

A 12-year-old boy fell out of a fifth-floor window in Nanchang, China, last Saturday. He survived by landing on a car parked below. His father believes the boy was sleepwalking when he fell. A hotel worker across the road heard a loud noise at midnight and thought it was a car crash.

Red Wings player Drew Miller is happy to be back on the ice. He got a bad cut on his face just a day ago that almost hurt his eye. Miller said he feels very lucky the skate didn't hit his eye. He had to wear a full face mask during practice. The cut was very deep and needed 50 to 60 stitches to close. He has a scar across his eye, but doctors say he did not damage his eyesight.

Filipe Luis wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends, even though Atletico Madrid wants to bring him back. He signed a three-year deal last July, but has had trouble keeping his spot as the left back. Atletico hope this gives them an advantage, but Luis says he is happy at Chelsea and wants to stay.

A 20-year-old Reading fan named Charlie Sumner ran onto the pitch without a shirt and did four somersaults during his first game ever at Madejski Stadium. This happened during a 3-0 FA Cup win over Bradford City last month. Because of this stunt, Sumner is now facing a three-year ban from football.

A video has emerged showing a group of men riding on top of a van being thrown off as the vehicle swerved around a corner. About half a dozen people were sitting on the roof of the van on a road near Salé, Morocco, when the vehicle tipped onto its side at high speed. The terrifying footage was filmed by a car following the van, which was carrying football fans. The video shows the packed vehicle weaving from side to side on what appears to be a dual carriageway before it toppled.

England has been drawn in Group D with the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy at the UEFA Under 17 European Championships. The tournament takes place in Bulgaria in May. John Peacock's Young Lions are the defending champions; they won last year's final in Malta against Holland on penalties. To advance to the quarter-finals, England must overcome the Dutch again. This is the first time the tournament has been expanded from eight to 16 nations. Danny Collinge scored his first England goal against Norway during qualifying and celebrated by running away.

An angry elephant tried to spray a buffalo bull with water from its trunk because the bull got too close. The elephant was relaxing in Kruger National Park in South Africa with its family near a small pool. In a video, the elephant squirts water, but misses the bull. The frustrated elephant tries again, while its young calf stays close for safety as the bull drinks from the pool.

Michael Thorpe, a former pub landlord, had his conviction overturned after eight years. He was found guilty in 2006 for showing a Premier League game on foreign TV channels at his pub in Plymouth without the proper permission. As a result of the legal battle, Mr. Thorpe lost his pub.

The Irish Football Association is worried that damage at their home stadium in Belfast might stop them from hosting a key soccer game against Romania in June.

Cracks were found in the West Stand of Windsor Park on Tuesday morning. The area was closed off while engineers checked the damage. The Irish FA found out about the problem on Tuesday. The damage happened overnight on Monday.

A 20-year-old football fan named Charlie Sumner has been banned for three years. He ran onto the pitch without a shirt and did somersaults during his first ever game at Reading's Madejski Stadium. This happened during an FA Cup quarter final replay with Bradford City while his team was winning 3-0. Sumner did four front flips, landing on his back each time, before stewards tackled him.

A BMW driver with five children in the car was arrested today after a university student was knocked down and killed while walking to the library. Hina Shamim, 21, died near Kingston University in London last night. She was just weeks away from turning 22. Friends left flowers at the scene and said she was "much-loved and the most charming girl in the world." Hina was killed after she was hit by the car as she walked home to the library.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested after a video of them fighting with a student at a high school was posted online. The incident happened at Langham Creek High School in Houston on Tuesday. The mother was reportedly angry because she believed the student had been bullying her daughter. In the video, the mother is seen wearing a black top on the right, and the student she fought is in the center wearing white.

Stoke's chief executive, Tony Scholes, wants to keep goalkeeper Asmir Begovic. Begovic is 27 and has one year left on his contract. He has been linked with other clubs, but Scholes believes Stoke can meet his ambitions. Scholes said Begovic is a great goalkeeper and the club wants to keep him. He added that it is normal for good players to have speculation about their future.

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand was caught reading a newspaper while driving. A passenger filmed the driver turning his head to look at the paper while the bus was moving. The passenger sent the video to the bus company, Ritchies Coachlines. The company's boss, Andrew Ritchie, called the driver a "complete idiot" and said he was embarrassed by what happened.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says Winston Reid will play against Leicester City on Saturday. Reid, who is from New Zealand, was injured in a game against Chelsea on March 4 but has now returned to full training.

However, Enner Valencia will not play. The Ecuadorian striker missed the last two games because of a toe injury he got at home in mid-March. Allardyce says Valencia is still not fit enough to play.

Five days before Brittany Huber and John Redman were to get married last May, a bad car crash on a Georgia highway killed the bride and left her fiance fighting for his life. Redman survived, but his doctors told him he would likely spend the rest of his life in a nursing home, stuck in a wheelchair. The future looked very bleak for the 25-year-old assistant basketball coach at Dalton State College. However, against all odds, Redman recovered. On March 24, he helped lead his team to win a championship title.

Lucas (left) and Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard played in a charity game at Anfield on Sunday. Lucas Leiva is trying to return to his best form after recovering from injury. He had played 16 games in a row from late November, which helped Liverpool win more matches. However, he missed 10 games in February after getting hurt during a derby match. He was on the bench before the international break, but he played the full 90 minutes in the charity game.

Japanese photographer Yûki Aoyama is tired of awkward father-daughter photos. To make them more interesting, he takes pictures of daughters leaping into the air while their fathers make dramatic poses. In the photos, the daughters smile at the camera while their fathers look serious. These pictures are from Aoyama's new book, which is roughly translated as "Daughter and Salary Man."

Police are looking for a man between 50 and 60 years old who robbed a bank in Cardiff in broad daylight. The robbery happened at 12:30pm at a Lloyds Bank in Fairwater. The man is about 5ft 9in to 6ft tall and was wearing black clothes. He has greying black hair and wore glasses. He ran away with about £3,000 in cash. Police have released CCTV images of him inside the bank and say no one was hurt. They believe the public can help identify him.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has removed Morocco's ban from the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments. The Confederation of African Football had originally banned Morocco from the 2017 and 2019 tournaments and fined the country $1 million. The CAF also asked for $9 million in compensation because Morocco pulled out of the tournaments due to fears about the Ebola epidemic. Morocco had pulled out as host of the tournament, which was eventually won by Ivory Coast in Equatorial Guinea. Now, Morocco can compete in the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments.

Tom Boyd thinks Jason Denayer’s loan at Celtic has been very successful. Because of this, Denayer is ready to try to play for Manchester City next season. This would stop Celtic manager Ronny Deila from keeping Denayer for another year. However, Boyd thinks this is a good thing. He believes Denayer’s success at Celtic will encourage other young players to join the team. Jason Denayer, a 19-year-old defender, has played well for Celtic this season. He also recently played for the Belgium national team in a qualifying game.

Andros Townsend scored a great goal for England in Italy, silencing people who doubted him. This season has been up and down for the 23-year-old, who hasn't played as well as he did when he first joined the national team. England manager Roy Hodgson believed in Townsend, and the Tottenham winger showed his belief was justified with an amazing strike. Townsend scored England's equalizer in their 1-1 friendly match against Italy in Turin on Tuesday. He celebrated his goal with his Tottenham teammates Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Chinese company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought 20% of Spanish soccer team Atletico Madrid. The deal was finalized on Tuesday at a special meeting where Wanda Madrid Investment signed the papers to buy 726,707 shares for €45 million (about £32.8 million). The purchase was first announced in January, but two special meetings were needed to make it official. Wanda Group chairman Wang Jianlin wants to help Atletico grow its brand in Asia. Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone talks to the media.

Antonio Conte said his return to Turin for Italy's 1-1 draw against England made him feel nostalgic, despite reports he received death threats before the game. He took over as Italy's manager in August, replacing Cesare Prandelli after Italy failed the World Cup group stage last summer. His time in charge has been inconsistent. Italy needed a late goal from Eder to tie 2-2 with Bulgaria last Saturday, and Conte reportedly received death threats from Juventus fans after Claudio Marchisio injured his knee the day before the Euro 2016 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that a simpler schedule could help Hibernian take second place from Rangers in the final month of the Championship season. His Dumbarton team has played both sides already this year and will face them again before the season ends. Although Rangers are currently winning, Murray believes they might struggle to keep up their current pace, and he expects the competition to shift back toward Hibernian.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet returned to England after playing for Belgium in Euro 2016 qualifying games. Although he was in the match squads for the games against Cyprus and Israel, he did not play. Chelsea's Thibaut Courtois was chosen instead. Mignolet shared photos of himself sitting in an aeroplane cockpit on his Facebook page.

A large country estate with a historic house and five cottages is for sale at £6 million. It is near Bridgnorth in Shropshire and sits on 200 acres of land. The property includes a swimming pool, tennis court, stables, and a cricket green. The main house, Chyknell Hall, has 11 bedrooms and was built in 1814. It has only been sold twice before. The secluded location offers complete privacy, making it attractive to wealthy buyers.

Two Dallas college police officers have been put on leave after video showed them harassing students and arresting one after hitting him. The incident happened at El Centro College last Wednesday. Student Charles Adams recorded the video while waiting for a bus outside the campus. The officers approached a group of high school students waiting for the bus.

Gary Locke has been made the permanent manager of Kilmarnock. He signed a three-year contract after working as an assistant manager last season. Locke took over the team in February and has only lost one game in the seven matches since then. He will speak to the media at a press conference on Friday morning.

This weekend, one of the biggest games in German football takes place. "Der Klassiker" is the name of the match between Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich. These two teams have won the last five Bundesliga titles together. Bayern Munich is expected to keep winning this season.

However, the teams are not equal right now. Bayern is much higher in the standings, with 31 points and nine more positions than Dortmund. Even with this gap, the game is still very important. These two teams always play a high-stakes match. Jurgen Klopp celebrates with the Dortmund players after they beat Hannover.

A 14-year-old girl named Deva Joseph was left stuck at London Stansted airport. easyJet would not let her board her flight to Spain because she had two pieces of hand luggage. Deva started crying and tried to pay to put the extra bag in the hold, but the airline only accepted credit cards. Since she is a teenager, she does not have a credit card.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed his grandfather John Potts, 45, with one very hard punch to the back of the head. The punch was so strong it made a loud cracking sound. Robson had been drinking after the funeral. He hit John Potts outside a sports bar to break up a fight. Sadly, Mr. Potts fell down and died. Robson, who has a history of violence, was sentenced to three and a half years in prison.

Thursday night was a great night for Notts County star Ellen White. She scored a goal and executed a perfect set-piece against her old team, Arsenal, in the Women's Super League.

In the 26th minute, Notts County was awarded a free kick near the edge of the box. Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood appeared to get confused and almost ran into each other. Ellen White took advantage of the confusion. She spun around on the edge of the box and hit the ball into the corner, scoring against her former club.

Although the girls are teenagers, the knives they use are not real; they are fake props.

We spend about a third of our lives sleeping. However, many people do not get the rest they need to feel refreshed. A study by the Sleep Health Foundation found that 30 percent of Australians complain about not getting enough sleep every day. According to Professor David Hillman, people need to make up for lost sleep to function well throughout the week. On average, adults need about eight hours of sleep per night, with a recommended range of seven to nine hours.

A video posted on Facebook shows a fight between neighbours in a Perth suburb. In the video, an angry woman yells racist insults at a group of men through her fence. She then goes into her neighbour's yard with a metal crowbar, shouting abuse and swinging the weapon at them. The men fight back with their own weapons. The woman returns to the yard, continuing to shout insults and swing the crowbar, yelling, "I don't deal with monkeys, go on now you f*****g monkeys."

Everyone is watching Valencia’s 19-year-old left back Jose Luis Gaya. Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea want to sign him this summer. They are trying to get him away from Real Madrid.

Sportswriter Pete Jenson looks at the Spain under-21 defender. Why do English clubs want him? His buy-out price is £13.5m. For comparison, Luke Shaw, a similar player, cost £27m. It would be foolish not to be interested, but there are also questions about if he is good enough for the Premier League.

Jose Luis Gaya played for Valencia in a La Liga match against Sevilla earlier this season.

Police in Oregon are asking the public to help find a motorcyclist who saved two teenagers. A man named Edward West, 59, allegedly pointed a gun at the teens in Salem and told them "get ready to die." A stranger on a green motorcycle stepped in and used his helmet to knock the gun away, letting the teens run away.

Tim Sherwood has asked Ron Vlaar to show his best form now that he is fit again and will lead Aston Villa. Sherwood wants Vlaar to help the team finish the season strongly. Vlaar played well for Holland in the World Cup in Brazil last year, even though they lost in a penalty shoot-out. Because of this, he has been linked with other clubs like Manchester United. On Saturday, Villa will play at Old Trafford, and Vlaar is fit to play and help the team try to avoid being relegated.

Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about a possible takeover of Aston Villa. He plans to build a team for next season if the club stays in the league. Randy Lerner is currently talking to people who might buy the club. If a new owner takes over, people might question Sherwood's job. But Sherwood is focused on keeping Villa in the league first. He will then make plans for the summer break. Christian Benteke scored a goal when Villa beat Sunderland last month.

Celtic really wants Manchester City to let Jason Denyer stay on loan for another season. However, City's manager, Manuel Pellegrini, says his young players are not ready for the main team yet. Because of this, Denyer might have to go back to City soon. Denyer has done well while playing for Celtic on loan from City this season.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting for a better date for Fraser Forster's return before deciding if he needs to sign a new goalkeeper this summer. Forster injured his knee during a 2-0 win over Burnley two weeks ago. Doctors say he could be back in four to 12 months. Koeman does not want to give a specific date yet and thinks Kelvin Davis can fill in, but he may bring in a new keeper if Forster takes longer to recover.

Steve Evans, the manager of Rotherham, was very angry on the sidelines. His team, who are in danger of being relegated, felt they should have been given a penalty during their narrow defeat in the Championship at Birmingham.

Birmingham took the lead in the first half with goals from Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson. Matt Derbyshire scored for Rotherham later in the game. However, just before the hour mark, Rob Kiernan handled the ball near the box while Matt Derbyshire was attacking. The referee, Dean Whitestone, did not give a penalty, much to the anger of the Rotherham manager. Robert Tesche of Birmingham City celebrated scoring the first goal of the match.

Holland’s national team coach, Guus Hiddink, has not contacted Celtic defender Virgil van Dijk. Van Dijk has played well for his club, but he was not chosen for the national team. This is strange because Holland has conceded many goals in recent qualifying games. Even though Van Dijk was selected for the national team twice last year, he was left out again when the team played Turkey. He was even vacationing in the Arabian Gulf at that time instead of playing for his country.

Celtic have complained to the Scottish Football Association about ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final at Hampden this month.

The game is against Inverness and will be played on Sunday, April 18 at 12.15pm. Ticket prices are £23 for the North and South stands, £15 for adults in the East Stand, and £5 for concessions.

Rangers interim chairman Paul Murray said on Thursday night that previous board members are solely to blame for the club being removed from the stock exchange. Because the club could not find a new advisor to meet regulations, they will have to leave the Alternative Investment Market. Murray insists this change will not affect the new board's plans or any planned investments.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were upset because they started the game against Italy poorly on Tuesday night. It was a friendly match at the Juventus Stadium, nine months after they met at the World Cup. England had won seven games in a row, but they struggled in the first half. Italy’s Graziano Pelle scored a header, putting the Italians ahead 1-0. Wayne Rooney, the England captain, tried to give instructions during the game. He said the team was upset by their first half performance, but they eventually drew 1-1.

Dundee United have responded to criticism from two major fan groups. Arabtrust and the Federation of Dundee United Supporters Clubs are upset that 25% of the £6.3 million transfer fees for Ryan Gauld, Andrew Robertson, Stuart Armstrong, and Gary Mackay-Steven were paid as commission to unknown parties. The groups also disagreed with chairman Stephen Thompson's claim about how much money he has invested in the club. The board says the criticism is wrong because the team has been successful on the field.

Gary Locke will be announced as Kilmarnock's permanent manager on Friday. He was originally asked to take charge until the end of the season, but the club has now given him a three-year contract.

The announcement will be made by the Rugby Park club on Friday morning. Locke, 39, has won the favor of new chairman Jim Mann because of the hard work of the players since he replaced Allan Johnston as a caretaker manager in February.

Chinese parents love raising child prodigies, like 10-year-old university students or four-year-olds who copy Michael Jackson dance moves. Now, a new young basketball star is becoming popular in China. A viral video shows a small boy with amazing basketball skills that beat many professional players. The five-year-old boy is named Mai Zizhuo. He has been playing basketball since he was two and a half, reported People's Daily Online. The video starts with him scoring many hoops, and then running around while dribbling two basketballs at once.

Bayern Munich will be without left-back David Alaba for the rest of the season. He was injured during a game for Austria against Bosnia and has a torn knee ligament. This is a serious injury; he was previously out for three months with a similar injury in his other knee. Alaba, 22, said he is disappointed but wants to play in the final game of the season.

Hull KR have signed Australian forward Dane Tilse to replace Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey. Tilse, who is 6ft 7in and weighs 17st-plus, has agreed to a two-and-a-half-year contract. He will join the team as soon as he gets the necessary paperwork, after Canberra Raiders agreed to let him go. Tilse, 30, has played 200 games in Australia and will link up with new captain Terry Campese. He is a direct replacement for Weyman, who retired last month due to injury.

Livingston boss Mark Burchill thinks midfielder Darren Cole will play in Sunday's Petrofac Cup final, even though his cousin recently died. Darren's cousin, Shaun Cole, 22, was found dead in a Miami street last weekend. Police believe he was hit by a car while walking. Shaun was a soldier who had served in Afghanistan and was on holiday in Florida. He had been to a music festival before he was found hurt on the pavement. Mark Burchill hopes Darren will play on Sunday.

Alan Smith has denied claims that Liverpool fans attacked the ambulance he was in after he was injured during a match nine years ago.

Smith broke his leg and dislocated his ankle while trying to block a free-kick by John Arne Riise in a fifth round FA Cup game at Anfield in February 2006. At the time, reports said that Liverpool fans tried to stop the ambulance from taking Smith to hospital by throwing bottles, beer glasses, and stones at the vehicle, and by rocking it.

Celtic wants to sign Danny Wilson, the captain of Hearts, this summer. Sportsmail reported that Celtic might offer £400,000 for the defender. Wilson has one year left on his contract with Hearts. The club's owner, Ann Budge, says they do not need to sell him. Wilson is a free agent at the end of the season.

Ronny Deila says Celtic will not play many games before the Champions League season starts because it is too tiring. He blamed last summer's trip to the US, Austria, and Germany for a 4-1 loss to Legia Warsaw. Celtic makes a lot of money from these trips and has visited Australia and Asia recently. Ronny Deila and Nir Bitton left the field after the loss. A trip to America this July is still possible.

Franck Ribery says reports linking Kevin de Bruyne with Bayern Munich are wrong. De Bruyne, who plays for Wolfsburg, has had a great season with nine goals and 16 assists. However, Ribery believes the 23-year-old Belgian is not the right fit to replace him or Arjen Robben because he plays differently.

The girlfriend of an Arizona State University football player has recanted her story. She originally accused him of abuse, but now says she lied because of mood swings.

Davon Durant, a linebacker at ASU, was arrested in March after his girlfriend, Kelsi Langley, claimed he hit her and grabbed her neck in his car. Following the arrest, Durant was suspended from the football team indefinitely. He transferred to ASU from a Kansas college and was a five-star recruit, and he could face expulsion.

Meeting your idol is exciting. Meeting them at Starbucks, wearing a shirt with their name, and having your photo posted on their Instagram is even better.

One little boy got to experience this with Justin Verlander. He is a pitcher for the Detroit Tigers. Verlander took a selfie with the boy. The boy was wearing a dark blue shirt. On the back of the shirt, his name "Verlander" and his jersey number "35" were written.
