Eden Hazard said that playing too many games for Chelsea made him too tired to play his best during Belgium's win over Israel on Tuesday. He has played 48 games this season for his club and country, missing only five matches for Chelsea. He was an important player as Chelsea chased the Premier League title. However, during the game against Israel, Hazard struggled to get past the opposing player Orel Dgani, and the manager Marc Wilmots took him off the field with 28 minutes remaining.

Police found 20 grams of marijuana hidden inside a leg of lamb in the Northern Territory. The police noticed a suspicious smell coming from the Northern Substance Abuse Intelligence Desk. Officers x-rayed the lamb and found the drugs. The lamb had been shipped to a company at Darwin Airport and was meant to be sent to the Tiwi Islands.

Troubled footballer Clarke Carlisle has revealed he has split from his wife. He is continuing to battle depression after he tried to kill himself in December. Mr. Carlisle, a former Premier League defender, said he moved out of the home he shared with his wife of 14 years, Gemma. He tried to kill himself two days after he was arrested for drink-driving.

Arsenal legend Paul Merson has changed his mind and admitted he was wrong to criticize Andros Townsend's England call-up. Townsend came off the bench to score a goal in Tuesday's 1-1 draw with Italy in Turin. This goal was the perfect response after Merson had previously said in his column, "If Andros Townsend can get in (the England squad) then it opens it up for anybody."

Cesc Fabregas, a midfielder for Chelsea, is having a difficult time this season. He played poorly in Spain's 2-0 loss to Holland on Tuesday. Although he was happy in London earlier this week, his performance has gotten much worse. Earlier in the year, around Christmas, he was playing very well and was expected to break the Premier League record for assists.

Six people have been arrested in Dover on suspicion of Syria-related terrorism offences, according to West Midlands Police. Five men and one woman were detained at around 8am this morning in the departure zone of the port. Four of the men, all in their 20s, are from Birmingham, West Midlands. A 26-year-old man and a 23-year-old woman with no fixed address were also held. They are currently being questioned at a police station in the West Midlands area.

Get ready to dig deep - the urge to buy a treat peaks today at 12:52pm. A study claims that Britons spend an average of £62 a week rewarding themselves, with retail therapy reaching a high at lunchtime today. Treats can range from as little as a bar of chocolate or a glass of wine to designer clothes and shoes, according to research by website VoucherCodes.co.uk. A study reveals that Britons spend an average of £62 a week on rewarding themselves, with retail therapy reaching a high at lunchtime today. Treats can range from a bar of chocolate to a glass of wine. And surprisingly, men spend a third more a month than women on treating themselves.

Arsene Wenger is a very respected and clearly intelligent man. Sometimes, you find yourself nodding at what he says because it sounds right. However, closer examination shows it has weak foundations.

Usually, this relates to how Arsenal’s defensive record is actually very good statistically. But last week, he talked about quotas. Specifically, he discussed FA chairman Greg Dyke’s idea to increase the number of homegrown players in a Premier League squad of 25 from eight to 12.

Charlie Austin and Joey Barton are now good friends. On Austin's first day at Queens Park Rangers, Barton ignored him. Austin later scored 15 goals in the Premier League this season. He is being considered for an England debut in the future.

This is a true story. A black dog saved his owner from a dangerous situation at the Clarence J. Brown Dam and Reservoir in Springfield, Ohio, on Saturday.

The man had gotten stuck waist-deep in mud while trying to recover some duck hunting gear. He had been in the cold, muddy water for almost two hours, and the water was nearly freezing.

The dog took a rescue rope to his owner. Firefighters then used the rope to pull the man to safety from the shore. The man had called 911 on his cell phone for help, but first responders could not use a boat because the river was too shallow.

Juventus coach Massimiliano Allegri says he won't be fully liked by the fans until the team wins the league. He started this job last summer, several months after being fired by AC Milan. Since then, he has done well, and Juventus is leading the race to win the Scudetto. On Saturday, Juventus will try to win three more points when they play Empoli at home.

When a team is playing well, it only takes a short time to score. Nathan Redmond had only been on the field for six minutes when he helped decide the game. Steven Whittaker passed the ball to Redmond on the right side. The ball stayed close to the white line as it moved forward. Redmond ran very fast and got past Joe Bennett. He then crossed the ball, and Bradley Johnson hit it into the net at the back post. Bradley Johnson scored the winning goal in the second half at the Amex Stadium.

Residents of Celoron, New York, are upset about a statue of their hometown icon, Lucile Ball. The statue, unveiled in 2009, looks so unlike the comedian that people are shocked and angry. A Facebook page called 'We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue' has over 600 supporters. The statue shows Ball drunk and pitching a health tonic from her TV show 'I Love Lucy.' Residents say the statue looks 'monstrous.'

South Sydney hooker Issac Luke is in trouble for a homophobic comment he posted on social media. He responded to Canterbury Bulldogs fans who had attacked him. On Saturday, Luke asked for help finding a young Rabbitohs fan who was allegedly attacked at ANZ Stadium in Sydney. The fan was hurt and went to the hospital. Luke wanted to give the fan his jersey to make up for what happened, but the comment he posted caused more problems.

A man in Wangaratta, northeast Victoria, was shocked when a large huntsman spider crawled out of his car door handle. He was spraying the door with insect repellent when the spider appeared. He told the spider to "get out," but he jumped back in fright when the spider's legs came out.

Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino says Harry Kane is like Gabriel Batistuta. He says he will help Kane if he struggles.

Kane recently moved close to scoring 30 goals in a season. He scored just 79 seconds after coming into a game against Lithuania. England manager Roy Hodgson says they should not expect too much from Kane yet. Kane became a regular player at Tottenham after being loaned out to Leicester and Norwich.

A former footballer who ran a £30 million investment scheme and lived like a millionaire is now 'surviving on handouts', a court was told. Michael McIndoe, who played for Bristol City and Wolverhampton Wanderers, convinced other footballers to invest by promising a 20% return. However, the scheme collapsed because of mounting debts, and the tricky winger was declared bankrupt in October last year with over £2 million in debts. Known as 'Mr Big' in Marbella, where he partied with glamorous women, the footballer is now being chased by creditors through the courts.

Juventus director Pavel Nedved said Barcelona want to sign Paul Pogba. In an interview, the former midfielder, who played 324 games for Juventus, said Pogba will not move. However, Nedved was happy Juventus did not play Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals.

A 48-year-old man named James Oliver was hit by a car driven by his girlfriend, Linda Currier, 53. Police say Oliver was injured after Currier hit him with the car in the driveway of a home in Noblesboro, Maine. Authorities say Currier hit Oliver after she caught him trying to sexually assault a 12-year-old girl inside the house.

Liverpool is interested in signing Fiorentina goalkeeper Neto. However, PSG and Spanish clubs also want him. His agent says Brendan Rodgers will have a hard time getting the deal done. Neto's contract runs out in June. Liverpool was linked with him earlier this year when Simon Mignolet was dropped. A winter move didn't happen, but Neto is likely to leave Fiorentina in the summer. He is 25 years old and previously played for Atletico Paranaense. In a game against Roma in March, Neto ran out of his goal while Juan Iturbe attacked.

A YouTube video shows a Porsche Cayman crashing on Prince Edward Island in Canada. The car was speeding when the light turned green, and it swerved out of control. It hit a concrete median, and a wheel came off. The driver, Richard Stewart, says having an expensive car does not make someone a good driver. He warns parents not to let their sons drive their Porsches.

Here is the information for Sunday's Sunderland vs Newcastle game:

Sunderland's midfielder Lee Cattermole will start the match. He is back after serving a two-match ban for getting five yellow cards this season.

If Rory McIlroy wins the Masters tournament, he will complete a lifelong goal to become the best golfer in the world. Working with his sponsor Bose, McIlroy made a video about his life. The video shows his start playing golf as a child and his rise to the top of the sport. It also shows some hard times he had. The video starts with McIlroy going for a run at sunrise. On the screen, the words 'Six weeks to Georgia' appear. The video also has an interview with a young Rory McIlroy.

Sergio Garcia says he is focused on winning his first PGA Tour title since 2012 at the Shell Houston Open. This is happening even though the Masters tournament is very close. Rory McIlroy is trying to win a third major in a row to complete the career grand slam. There is also a question about whether Tiger Woods will return from his self-imposed break. However, the Golf Club of Houston is set up to look like Augusta. Despite this, Garcia is only concentrating on ending his victory drought. He lined up a putt during the Cadillac Championship in Doral, Florida last month.

Riki Hughes, a veteran of the Iraq war, volunteered as the club secretary for Tidworth Town Football Club. He stole £17,000 from the club's accounts. Hughes claimed he was paying rent to the club's landlord, but the team actually got the property for free. He used the stolen money to buy camping equipment and take a stag holiday to Las Vegas. Hughes was sentenced to 16 months in jail.

Johnny Sexton is used to success. He adds gold medals to his collection every year. As he gets ready for a big game with Saracens in Paris, the Racing Metro player reflected on his winning habit.

'I’ve been very lucky to play for great teams with Leinster and Ireland,' he said. 'There haven't been many years that have gone by that I haven't been part of a side winning trophies.' In fact, since he started playing senior rugby in 2010, 2010 is the only year he did not win anything.

Mustafa Kamal quit his job as ICC president on Wednesday. He is from Bangladesh. He said India used its position to change the result of the Cricket World Cup match between Bangladesh and India. He told reporters at the airport that everyone saw what happened in that game. He said he would have reacted the same way if it had happened to any other country. He is seen with the Cricket World Cup trophy.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce likes Leicester City boss Nigel Pearson. He thinks Pearson is "his own man."

Allardyce worked with Pearson at Newcastle United in 2007. They will see each other on Saturday when West Ham plays Leicester.

Pearson has had some angry moments this season. He grabbed Crystal Palace player James McArthur by the throat, and he shouted at a reporter during a press conference.

Skipper John O'Shea has told Sunderland they must win to control their own future. Sunderland and Newcastle meet at the Stadium of Light on Sunday. Sunderland has won the last four games in a row, but they need three points to move away from the bottom of the league. If Burnley beats Tottenham earlier on Sunday, Sunderland could end up in the relegation zone. Therefore, winning is very important for the team.

Mark Hughes, the manager of Stoke City, really wants his team to stop losing to Chelsea. Since Stoke got promoted to the top English league in 2008, they have played Chelsea away eight times and lost every single game. Their last win at Chelsea was way back in 1995. Their most recent game at Stamford Bridge ended in a 3-0 loss for Stoke, with Frank Lampard celebrating Chelsea's victory.

Newcastle will play Sunderland in a key derby match on Sunday. They are trying to avoid losing three games in a row. The team has struggled recently because their top striker, Papiss Cisse, is banned. Sunderland are currently near the bottom of the league table. However, Sportsmail reports that without Cisse’s goals, Newcastle would be two points lower in the standings. Cisse is Newcastle’s best player this season, having scored 11 goals, 10 of which helped his team win.

Dick Advocaat will bring back Lee Cattermole to the middle of his Sunderland team. Cattermole, 27, has been suspended for the last two games because he reached 10 bookings this season. He missed Advocaat's first game, a 1-0 loss at West Ham on March 21.

However, Cattermole is guaranteed to start against Newcastle on Sunday. Advocaat wants a strong response from a player who has missed much of the season due to injury.

For Ronny Deila, playing in the Champions League is not just about the money. However, there are now 16 million reasons for him to lead Celtic there by winning a fourth straight title, as all of those reasons involve cash.

This week, UEFA confirmed their 'cash cycle' for the next three years of European competition. The last time Celtic reached the Champions League group stage, in 2013-14 when they faced AC Milan, Ajax, and Barcelona, they won one match and earned £12.6 million. If they perform the same or better next season, that sum would rise by £4 million. If they reach the last 16, the money would crash through the £20 million barrier. This is even before they count ticket

Tottenham defender Ben Davies will play against his Wales teammate Sam Vokes at Burnley on Sunday. Spurs are going to Turf Moor after winning three of their last four Premier League games, hoping to keep their chance of playing in Europe next season alive. Burnley are currently 18th in the league, just one point above the relegation zone. Earlier this season, Vokes scored for Burnley against Tottenham in the FA Cup, and Davies turned away in disappointment following the equaliser.

Neil Redfearn is thinking about his job as manager of Leeds United. This comes after the club suspended his assistant, Steve Thompson, on Thursday.

Leeds United hired Thompson two months ago. However, yesterday, director of football Nicola Salerno sent him a letter saying he is suspended until the end of the season. This effectively ends his time at the club after 105 days.

Thompson has been told he will be suspended until his contract expires. He has also been told the club will not renew his contract.

John Carver says he will use a whip to motivate his Newcastle players before Sunday's Tyne-Wear derby at the Stadium of Light. The Magpies have lost four matches in a row against their North-East rivals. Carver, who was assistant to Alan Pardew during that losing streak, admits that Sunderland wanted victory more than Newcastle on those occasions. 'In the last four games Sunderland have out-worked us - and that's not a good stat to have,' he said.

David Templeton has criticized the training methods used at Rangers by Ally McCoist and Kenny McDowall. He said former player Stuart McCall brings better coaching and tactics. Templeton praised McCall since he started the job last month, noting two wins have boosted confidence before Saturday's game against Hearts.

Nolito, a forward for Celta Vigo, wants Lionel Messi to stay away from Sunday's game. He says Messi should spend the day at the beach instead of playing, because Messi is recovering from a foot injury. Nolito even said he will call Messi's dad to tell him to keep the star player home. However, Messi is expected to be fit to play after training with his teammates.

Robbie Neilson says captain Danny Wilson will only leave Hearts if he thinks it is the right decision for the club. This week, Celtic were linked with a move for the former Rangers defender. Neilson admitted that other teams are likely to want his promoted players this summer. However, he will only let them go if the price is right and he agrees it is the best move for Hearts.

Sam Allardyce has warned Brendan Rodgers that giving Raheem Sterling a big new contract could cause problems for the rest of the Liverpool team. The West Ham manager feels that paying Sterling more than the £100,000-per-week deal he was already offered would lead to his team-mates demanding higher wages. Allardyce does not blame Sterling, who currently earns £35,000 a week, for trying to get a better deal. He feels there are very few talented young players emerging, so clubs are willing to pay huge wages to sign them. Raheem Sterling, a Liverpool and England star, has stalled over signing a new contract at Anfield.

Blackpool is trying to sign 25-year-old Austrian defender Thomas Piermayr. He has been training with the team this week. Piermayr is a free agent who was last playing for Colorado Rapids in the United States. He previously played for Inverness Caledonian Thistle in 2011. This move would be his first in English football.

Tony Pulis wants to talk to West Bromwich Albion chairman Jeremy Peace after the team stays in the Premier League. Pulis wants to make the club a top-ten team again. He says the team has "gone off the rails" recently and needs big changes. Last season, West Brom finished 17th after finishing 10th and 8th in previous years under other managers.

Ian Wright, a legend for Arsenal, is sad that Theo Walcott might leave the club. He thinks Walcott's problems are because manager Arsene Wenger does not play him as a striker. Walcott has only started five games this season after being injured for seven months. With Arsenal trying to sign Raheem Sterling and Walcott's contract ending next summer, Wright is worried the team might lose a good player.

Roberto Martinez is supporting Ross Barkley to improve at Everton and England. Barkley had a difficult season after playing in the World Cup and having knee surgery. However, England coach Roy Hodgson still believes in him. Martinez thinks Barkley’s recent substitute appearances for England show he is ready to play better.

England will not play in the Under 19 European Championships this summer. They lost 2-1 to France in their final qualifying match.

Earlier, England had beaten Denmark and Azerbaijan in the Elite Round. To reach the finals in Greece, they needed to beat France in Saint-Lo. France scored two goals from Sehrou Guirassy and Gnaly Cornet. England scored one goal late from Patrick Roberts of Fulham, but it was not enough to qualify.

Newcastle midfielder Jonas Gutierrez is hoping to celebrate his return to the team with a win over Sunderland. The 31-year-old Argentinian has played as a substitute in the last three games since returning from cancer. He has been welcomed back warmly. However, he has lost each of those games. He is desperate to end that run as Newcastle tries to stop a four-game losing streak against Sunderland on Sunday.

NRL referees and officials were hit with objects by angry fans after South Sydney beat Canterbury 18-17 in a close game at ANZ Stadium on Good Friday. With the score 18-17, the Rabbitohs won after the referee penalised Bulldogs captain James Graham in the last minute. After the game, as everyone walked toward the tunnel, a group of fans threw plastic water bottles and shouted abuse at the referees and players.

Former England rugby league captain Kevin Sinfield will leave his team at the end of the season to join Yorkshire Carnegie in rugby union. The 34-year-old, who is considered the best captain in Leeds Rhinos history, announced his shock move on Tuesday. He has signed an 18-month contract with the club.

Raheem Sterling, a 20-year-old player for Liverpool, has said he is not ready to sign a new contract. The club offered him a new deal worth £100,000 a week to stay, but he revealed in a BBC interview that he would have accepted less money a year ago.

Despite being a key player for Liverpool, Sterling has struggled to play well this season. He has scored only six goals, which is one less than Jon Walters of Stoke. His performance has gotten worse, as shown by his lower conversion rate and the amount of time he spends on the field for each goal he scores.

Brighton and Hove Albion are teaching their young players about the law and ethics of sexual consent. The Championship club is the first to offer this kind of training and counselling to its youth players, according to the BBC. The Protect, Inform and Prevent (PIP) programme explains when consent can legally be given. Part of the training involves confidential question and answer sessions about past encounters. These sessions are led by a former police detective and a psychotherapist.

A new video shows homeless people reading mean tweets written about them. The clip was made by a company called Leo Burnett Toronto for a charity named Humans For Humans. The video is meant to make people think about how they treat people who sleep on the street. Many of the people start to cry as they read mean comments, such as 'I hate the homeless' and 'I almost vomited' when seeing a homeless girl.

George Boyd is the Barclays Premier League's hardest working player. He ran 210.5 miles on the pitch this season. This is the same distance as running from Burnley's Turf Moor ground to Crystal Palace's Selhurst Park in south London. He ran slightly further than Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Christian Eriksen. Walking that journey usually takes 69 hours, but Boyd managed it in less than 40 hours of playing time.

Police are investigating the death of a five-month-old baby. The parents, a 25-year-old father and a 25-year-old mother from Perry Barr, Birmingham, have been arrested.

Emergency services were called to the family home just before 1:00 AM yesterday because the baby was having trouble breathing. The child was taken to Birmingham Children's Hospital, but sadly died this afternoon. Police are treating the death as suspicious and a post-mortem examination will be held today to determine the exact cause of death.

Gordon Taylor, the head of the players' union, says Raheem Sterling is not being disloyal to Liverpool. Sterling, 20, has put talks about a new contract on hold until the summer. Manager Brendan Rodgers made him an incredible offer of £100,000 a week, but negotiations have stopped. Sterling says he is not just chasing money, and Taylor believes waiting until the season ends to talk again is a smart idea. Sterling also told TV viewers that he is not ready to sign a new deal with Liverpool yet.

Manchester United flop Anderson has had a tough time since returning to Brazil, but on Wednesday his own mistake was overshadowed by his teammate's stupidity. The Brazilian midfielder was sent off for shoving an opponent. However, his teammate Fabricio stole the attention by swearing at the fans and getting a red card, leaving Internacional with only nine players in the 1-1 draw.

A seven-year-old boy was raped and set on fire by two youths. The youths took the boy to an isolated place and raped him. When he resisted, they set him on fire. The boy, who suffered 30 per cent burns to his body, somehow managed to escape. The shocking incident occurred in Pagma Nagar, in Bhiwandi City, a suburb of Mumbai. Police are investigating the incident.

A pug named Dug had a lucky escape after a rattlesnake bit him in the face. Dug and his owner, Lindsay Castro, were hiking on a trail in Fontana, Canada, on Thursday. They heard a rattling sound, and Lindsay moved back, but Dug ran toward the snake. The snake bit Dug in the face, and his face quickly swelled up to twice its normal size.

Jose Mourinho could one day return to manage Real Madrid, even though he left the club in 2013 under difficult circumstances. Real defender Alvaro Arbeloa says the door is open for the Chelsea manager to come back. Mourinho spent three years at Real Madrid before he left to rejoin Chelsea. His departure was controversial, with rumors of arguments with senior players like Iker Casillas, Sergio Ramos, and Pepe. However, Arbeloa believes Real Madrid would welcome Mourinho back as manager.

Liverpool and their manager Brendan Rodgers had a difficult day at the Emirates stadium on Saturday. Their hopes of playing in the Champions League next year ended in defeat. The manager faced the press and admitted that his team's title chances were over. Although Mr. Rodgers tried to stay positive, he admitted that this has been a tough season. Last year, the team fought hard for the championship, but this year they have fallen behind. It is a sad result for a club that wanted to return to winning ways. However, the team is still believed to be improving under the manager.

Angry Inter Milan coach Roberto Mancini cancelled his players' day off and ordered them to train early on Sunday. This happened after they drew 1-1 at home with bottom-placed Parma. Inter's website confirmed the team trained at 8:30 a.m. local time, watched by club vice-president Javier Zanetti and sporting director Piero Ausilio. Mancini was furious that the Saturday draw left the team joint ninth with Genoa, 10 points behind the European qualification spots.

Most fans want to own a rare piece of memorabilia from their favorite player or team. Small bits of history can sell for thousands of pounds on the open market.

However, you might be surprised to learn that an expired passport belonging to Paul Parker—most famous for playing right back for Manchester United and England in the nineties—was listed on eBay for £5,000. The item was listed earlier in March, and the bidding ended on Tuesday. It is unclear if anyone actually paid the large sum being quoted.

Ex-Manchester United and England defender Paul Parker’s old passport was listed on eBay.

A builder named Paddy Morrall saw a picture of Jesus Christ on a piece of wood in Inverness, Scotland. He found the wood, which was a broken scaffolding board, lying outside on Wednesday, just a few days before Easter. The image of Jesus appeared on the wood after it had been left in the rain for several hours. Mr. Morrall, who is 31 years old and lives near Bradford, has kept the piece of wood.

Ondrej Duda scored a goal in the second half to give Slovakia a 1-0 win over the Czech Republic on Tuesday. The 20-year-old midfielder hit a low shot from outside the penalty area in the 49th minute for his second goal for his country. This was Slovakia's third win in ten games since the countries split in 1993. Martin Skrtel hit Daniel Kolar in the face with his boot during the match. Slovakia celebrated the win, which continues their excellent recent form.

Real Madrid star Karim Benzema showed off his rapping skills in a new video. He was driving his Bugatti Veyron while singing along to Tupac's song 'Check Out Time'. This happened as Real Madrid prepared to play Granada at the Bernabeu stadium on Sunday. Benzema has scored 20 goals this season.

A businessman who helped force Liam Fox to resign is trying to defeat Conservative politicians. He has given £30,000 to Ukip to fight Fox in Somerset. He is also spending another £30,000 to try to beat Tom Tugendhat, a Conservative candidate in Kent.

Sheffield Wednesday and Huddersfield played to a 1-1 draw. In the 86th minute, substitute Sergiu Bus scored the first goal for Wednesday. Just before the game ended, substitute Ishmael Miller scored to tie the game for Huddersfield. This result means Huddersfield has not won in seven games and is in 18th place, six spots and nine points behind Wednesday.

Stuart Dallas has improved a lot since Mark Warburton found him playing part-time for £70 a week. The 23-year-old, who played for Northern Ireland, scored two great goals as Brentford beat Fulham 4-1 on Good Friday. They go into Monday's game against Nottingham Forest wanting more than just a play-off spot. Three years ago, Warburton spotted Dallas playing on a muddy field for Crusaders back home. Dallas has been a key player this season, helping Brentford push for promotion to the Premier League.

Baseball is very popular in America. Because of this, many people have strong feelings about their favorite professional team. The New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox are the most popular teams. They are rivals, and many people consider them the best. The Texas Rangers and Atlanta Braves also have many fans, especially in the South. However, some teams are not as popular. The New York Mets get less support than the other teams.

Trey Moses, a senior at Eastern High School in Louisville, Kentucky, asked his classmate Ellie Meredith to the prom. Moses, who volunteers with teenagers with learning disabilities, surprised Ellie during her P.E. class with flowers and a sign that said, "Let's Party Like it's 1989." This was a reference to a Taylor Swift album, which is Ellie's favorite. Ellie accepted the invitation and told CNN she is excited to go dress shopping.

On April Fools' Day, President Barack Obama pretended to be Frank Underwood, the fictional president from the TV show *House of Cards*.

"This is not Frank Underwood," the President said, turning his head. "This is Barack Obama. Happy April Fools' Day. Frank learned it from me."

President Obama used a southern accent to sound like Frank Underwood, who is played by actor Kevin Spacey and is known for giving long speeches to the camera.

Caykur Rizespor midfielder Ludovic Obraniak went to the hospital on Saturday after he felt sick during a game against Fenerbahce. The Poland player had to leave the field after only 30 minutes. The team said on social media that Obraniak was not in immediate danger after initial tests. He is currently on loan from the German team Werder Bremen. Fenerbahce player Moussa Sow scored a goal during their 5-1 win.

Three people went to the hospital after a crash between a vintage 1973 Jaguar and a Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night. The accident happened at a traffic light intersection on Warringah Road in Frenchs Forest, northern Sydney. The 1973 Jaguar, which was worth over $120,000, was completely destroyed. Although nobody was seriously hurt, all three adults were taken to the hospital as a precaution. Police are still investigating how the crash happened.

Villagers in Shandong Province, China, have started carrying natural gas in large plastic bags. People in Lijin village use rickshaws to transport the gas, which can be as long as six meters. Because the gas is very flammable, onlookers worry that a cigarette or flame could cause an explosion. Local media say this is done to save money on gas transportation.

Tiger Woods has been seen hitting balls at Augusta National, which increases the chances he will play in the first Major of the year. Woods has not played on the PGA Tour since he withdrew from the Farmers Insurance Open on February 5 because his back problems returned. He has taken time off to try and get better, but there is speculation he will return for the Masters, a tournament he has won four times. On Tuesday, Woods was spotted practicing at Augusta and is said to have returned to the course. He has dropped out of the top 100 golfers in the world for the first time in almost 19 years.

The BBC spent licence fee payers' money on a 44-page guide teaching staff how to use emojis. Executives hired an agency to research how to use smiley faces in news and on social media. Emoji designers also made graphics for stars like Gary Lineker and Graham Norton. The BBC used a 'sad face' emoticon to describe the death of the world's oldest woman.

One of the world's top distance runners and a training partner of Mo Farah says he is scared for his life. He told reporters that a coach in Uganda has been sexually abusing female runners, some as young as 15. Moses Kipsiro, who won the 10,000m at the Commonwealth Games last year, said five runners came to him for help. He claims he has received death threats after reporting the abuse to his national federation and the police.

Former Holland forward and assistant coach Patrick Kluivert has started his coaching job with a win. His team, Curacao, advanced to the second round of World Cup qualifying for 2018. They won 4-3 on aggregate after drawing 2-2 in a second match on Montserrat. Curacao also won 2-1 at home on Saturday. Kluivert, who used to play for Holland, helped the team progress. He previously worked as an assistant coach with Louis van Gaal at the 2014 World Cup.

An 18-year-old student was expelled from his fraternity, dropped out of college, and sent for a mental health check after he was filmed biting the head off a live hamster. DailyMail.com identified him as Brady Eaves, the stepson of a former Mississippi governor candidate, after he posted a video of the killing during a drunken Spring Break trip. The video, allegedly filmed in Florida, shows Eaves laughing as he killed the animal. He could face felony animal cruelty charges, which carry a possible five-year prison sentence and a $5,000 fine.

Sri Lanka's sports minister asked Kumar Sangakkara to keep playing limited overs cricket for one more year. Sangakkara had retired after a World Cup quarter-final loss on March 18. He said he was happy with how the team had improved since he started playing in 2000. The minister made the request after naming a new group to run the sport.

Edinburgh has three Scottish international players back for Sunday's European Challenge Cup game against London Irish. Dougie Fife, Alasdair Dickinson, and Ross Ford were rested last week during a 26-15 win over the Scarlets because they played in the RBS Six Nations. Coach Alan Solomons has recalled them to play at the Madejski Stadium, hoping to pick his best team. Dougie Fife is one of three Scottish players returning to Edinburgh after the Six Nations. England's Courtney Lawes was tackled by Scotland players Ross Ford, David Denton, and others.

Chris Ramsey says Tony Pulis is one of the best British coaches in the country. However, Ramsey says his team, QPR, does not need tactical advice from Pulis.

QPR plays West Brom at the Hawthorns on Saturday. QPR is 19th in the Premier League, four points behind Sunderland in 17th place. QPR has only four points since the start of the year.
